notes: Neighbourhood inferred from the name; confirm.
blurb: A conservative family Puja at 78 Nimtala Ghat Street, Hatkhola, in a house that is over 200 years old.
dishes: Nilkantha bird ritual to close the Puja

tips.expect: A traditional, old-Calcutta household Puja rather than a spectacle, with strict family rituals.
tips.good: The nilkantha (blue jay) ritual at the close of the Puja, when the birds are released to carry the goddess's message to Shiva.
tips.watch: Nimtala Ghat Street leads to the Ganga, so expect traffic restrictions and processions around Dashami.
tips.tip: Visit on Saptami or Ashtami morning for the most relaxed darshan.

blurb: A 170-year-old Puja at 15 Ramnath Kabiraj Lane, started by Rashmoni Dasi, with a rare ashtadhatu idol of Singhabahini.

tips.expect: A smaller, intimate house Puja in the Baghbazar lanes, with a family that also celebrates Kali Puja.
tips.good: The metal idol is unusual for the city, and the stained-glass decoration around the dalan is lovely in the evening.
tips.watch: The lanes are tight and unlit in places, so keep your phone torch handy after dark.
tips.tip: Pair with Baghbazar Sarbojanin, Kumartuli and Nobin Chandra Das for a very compact North Kolkata loop.

blurb: The Seal family's Puja at 42 Muktaram Babu Street, running since about 1855 in the Vaishnav tradition.

tips.expect: A beautifully decorated thakurdalan in a Vaishnav household, so no animal sacrifice and a gentler feel.
tips.good: Chorbagan has several old Puja houses on one street, so it is easy to see a few in a short walk.
tips.watch: Muktaram Babu Street is a busy business street by day, with little room to stand and look.
tips.tip: Combine with Chorbagan Mitra Bari next door and the Chorbagan Sarbojanin pandal.

blurb: The Mitra family house at 84 Muktaram Babu Street, built by the moneylender Ramsundar Mitra and said to be among the oldest Pujas in the city.
dishes: Gothic entrance with six large pillars

tips.expect: A grand old house with a Gothic-style pillared entrance that was renovated by Macintosh & Burn, and a long-running Durga and Kali Puja.
tips.good: The architecture is as much the draw as the Puja.
tips.watch: Claims of 300+ years are family tradition and I could not confirm them independently.
tips.tip: Good for a morning or afternoon visit when the street is quiet.

blurb: Dwarakanath Dutta started this Vaishnav-style Puja at 3 Bidhan Sarani in 1855. He is remembered for giving workers a Puja bonus.

tips.expect: A calm, traditional household Puja just off the Thanthania Kalibari, with no animal sacrifice.
tips.good: It is easy to reach and rarely packed, so you can take your time.
tips.watch: Bidhan Sarani itself is a very busy road, so cross carefully.
tips.tip: Pair it with a stop at Thanthania Kalibari and College Street for coffee.

blurb: The Roy family's Colootola Puja at 2A Gopal Chandra Lane, running since 1858 in a Vaishnav household that uses fruit for the symbolic sacrifice.
dishes: Arched thakur dalan with lamp-topped pillars

tips.expect: A handsome arched thakur dalan around a quadrangle, with side lighting that makes it glow at night. The puja moved briefly in 1946 and then returned.
tips.good: One of the prettiest dalans in North Kolkata after dark.
tips.watch: Colootola's lanes are tight, so don't try to bring a car.
tips.tip: Walk here from College Street or Central metro. Also called the Kolutolla Rajbari.

blurb: A Puja of 175 years or more at 4 Thakurdas Palit Lane, with a nicely decorated thakurdalan.

tips.expect: A modest, traditional house Puja in a tight Central Kolkata lane.
tips.good: The decorations around the thakurdalan.
tips.watch: Little is written about this house, so hours and access may differ from year to year.
tips.tip: Combine with Nilmani Mitra Bari and Rani Rashmoni Bari on one walk.

blurb: The Mitra family house at 19 Nilmoni Mitra Street, with a Puja started in 1809 by Radha Krishna Mitra.
dishes: Two nilkantha birds released at the end

tips.expect: A traditional old-Calcutta house Puja.
tips.good: The nilkantha ritual: one bird is sent toward Kailash and one towards the sky over Darjipara.
tips.watch: Google Maps pins this as Nilmani Dey's Thakur Bari, a few km south of Darjipara. It is a separate stop from Darjipara Mitra Bari.
tips.tip: Visit in daylight; the lanes are quiet and dark at night.

blurb: Rani Rashmoni's Janbazar mansion, at 13 Rani Rashmoni Road. The Puja here goes back to 1790 and Ramakrishna is said to have worshipped the goddess here in 1864.

tips.expect: A big 19th-century mansion where each branch of the family runs its own courtyard Puja. Rani Rashmoni also founded the Dakshineswar Kali Temple.
tips.good: The ekchala idol decorated with traditional daker saj, and how close it is to Esplanade metro.
tips.watch: Branches in different courtyards mean you may need to ask which entrance (the Free School Street side is one) leads to which Puja.
tips.tip: The easiest Bonedi Bari to add on to a Park Street or New Market evening.

blurb: The Radha Gobinda Mallick family Puja on Mohini Mohan Road, Bhowanipore, moved here in 1925 from an 1860 ancestral home. The family is also known for the film stars Ranjit and Koel Mallick.

tips.expect: South Kolkata's best-known Bonedi Bari, with a bigger crowd than most because of the family's celebrity connection.
tips.good: A real family Puja in the middle of South Kolkata, easy to combine with Bhowanipore food.
tips.watch: Expect queues on Ashtami and Navami evenings. Names like Mullick and Mallick are common, so check the address (Mohini Mohan Road).
tips.tip: Go on Saptami or Dashami for a thinner crowd.

blurb: The Sabarna Roy Choudhury family's Atchala Puja at 26 Sabarna Para Road, Barisha. Started in 1610, it is often called the oldest Durga Puja in the city.

tips.expect: A very old family Puja in Barisha, in the south-west. The Roy Choudhurys were the zamindars of the three villages that became Calcutta.
tips.good: The Atchala dalan and the sense of history. The original structure is still used to prepare the idol.
tips.watch: It is far from the other Baris, so don't try to fit it between two North Kolkata stops. The family runs pujas at several sites.
tips.tip: Give Behala its own half-day. Purple Line stations like Behala Chowrasta are the closest metro.

tips.expect: A Roy family house in Behala. I couldn't find reliable details.
tips.watch: It may be one of the Sabarna Roy Choudhury family's branch pujas in the Barisha area. Confirm before you go.
tips.tip: Visit it with the Atchala Bari in one Behala trip.

blurb: One of the two Deb mansions on Raja Nabakrishna Street. Nabakrishna Deb started the family Puja here in 1757 and famously hosted Robert Clive.

tips.expect: A large mansion with a pillared courtyard and a grand thakurdalan. This is the best known of all the Bonedi Baris, so it draws sightseers as well as devotees.
tips.good: The setting itself: the Natmandir, the lion gate, and the sense of being inside the Puja that shaped the city's Puja tradition.
tips.watch: Queues and foot traffic build up on Ashtami and Navami evenings, and the lanes around Raja Nabakrishna Street are narrow.
tips.tip: Go in the morning or early afternoon for a calm look. It is a short walk from Shobhabazar Sutanuti metro, so skip the car.

name.en: Shobhabazar Rajbari (Maharaja Naba Krishna Dev Bari)

blurb: The second Shobhabazar Rajbari, at 33 and 36 Raja Nabakrishna Street. The Deb family's Puja here dates to 1757.
dishes: A lion with a horse's face
Singi fish offered in place of goats (family legend)

tips.expect: Heritage architecture and a family Puja that is also a bit of a museum of old Calcutta. The two Shobhabazar houses stand close together, so you can see both in one go.
tips.good: The unusual lion with a horse's face, and the story behind the family's Clive-era Puja.
tips.watch: Rules at private houses vary: ask before photographing the idol or rituals.
tips.tip: Combine with the thakur dalan and Darjipara and Chatu Babu Latu Babu houses on foot.

blurb: The thakurdalan of the Shobhabazar Rajbari, the heart of the Deb family Puja since 1757.

tips.expect: The main worship hall, with the idol under the pillared arches of the courtyard.
tips.good: Evening lighting makes the arches and columns look their best.
tips.watch: Likely the same compound as the Rajbari entries above, so you may not need to count it as a separate stop.

blurb: Darjipara's Mitra house, a traditional household Puja in the Shobhabazar-Darjipara pocket.

tips.expect: A traditional household Puja in the Darjipara area.
tips.watch: A separate stop from Nilmani Mitra Bari, a few km away.
tips.tip: See the Shobhabazar Rajbaris first, then walk over.

blurb: Ramdulal Nibas at 67E Beadon Street, where Ram Dulal Dey began the Puja in 1770. His sons Asutosh (Chatu Babu) and Pramathanath (Latu Babu) gave the house its name.

tips.expect: A well-known house with a distinctive idol and plenty of visitors.
tips.good: It is on Beadon Street, close to Girish Park metro.
tips.watch: Beadon Street is a busy market road, and the evening crowd is thick.
tips.tip: A good first stop before the Jorasanko and Pathuriaghata houses.

notes: Goa Bagan, Maniktala (not Girish Park itself).
blurb: A Dutta family house at Goa Bagan, Maniktala, bought by Raghunath Dutt in 1922. The idol is of Hara-Parbati and the Puja feels like medieval Bengal.

tips.expect: A traditional, welcoming household Puja. The family serves lunch to more than 400 people every day until Dashami.
tips.good: The unusual Hara-Parbati idol and the community feel. The family is also known for its lantern festival at Kali Puja.
tips.watch: It sits in Maniktala, away from the Girish Park cluster on your list, so it needs its own short detour.
tips.tip: Go around lunchtime to see the community meal.

blurb: A 150-year-old Puja at 122A Maniktala Street, from a family that made its money in the salt trade.
dishes: White house with a big courtyard
White stone lions at the dalan entrance

tips.expect: A white mansion around a large courtyard, with stone lions at the thakurdalan.
tips.good: It photographs well in daylight and is rarely crowded.
tips.watch: Maniktala Main Road is busy, so stick to the footpath.
tips.tip: Combine with Bholanath Dham, Maniktala Chaltabagan and Hatibagan.

tips.expect: A family house Puja in the Girish Park and Jorasanko belt. I couldn't find reliable details online.
tips.watch: Check the address locally before you head over.
tips.tip: Ask at the neighbouring Daw and Dutta houses for directions.

blurb: Solicitor Shyamal Dhon Dutta started this Puja at Balaram De Street in 1882 to celebrate the birth of his first grandson.
dishes: Kumari Puja on Saptami, Ashtami and Navami

tips.expect: A traditional household Puja that starts early, from Krishna Nabami, and keeps up a Kumari Puja on three days. No animal sacrifice.
tips.good: Kumari Puja is the highlight, and the house is a short walk from Girish Park metro.
tips.watch: Balaram De Street is narrow and crowded in the evening.
tips.tip: Pair with the Daw houses and Harakutir for a good heritage walk.

blurb: The Daw family of Jorasanko, who ran the Narasimha Chandra Daw & Co. gun shop from 1835, gave this branch its 'Bandookwala' (gun seller) name.

tips.expect: A Jorasanko family Puja from a family with a business history, close to the Shib Krishna Daw house.
tips.good: Easy to see together with the other Daw house, and close to the Tagore house at Jorasanko.
tips.watch: The Daw family has more than one Puja, so make sure you have the right lane.
tips.tip: Do this and Jorasanko Daw Bari in one go.

blurb: The Daw house at 12A Shibkrishna Daw Lane. The Puja began in 1840 and its thakurdalan has been used for film shoots.

tips.expect: A beautifully kept thakurdalan with balconies around the courtyard, and an idol dressed in heavy gold and silver ornaments.
tips.good: The jewellery and the glittering chalchitra background are what visitors come for.
tips.watch: The Daw family has more than one Puja, so make sure you have the right lane. Daw Bari Bandook Wala is a separate house nearby.
tips.tip: Evening lighting is best for the ornaments.

dishes: Gold and silver ornaments on the goddess

blurb: A 271-year-old house built on what was once a cremation ground beside the Ganga. The family Puja is reported to date back to the late 1690s.

tips.expect: A very old, story-rich house with legends of hidden tunnels used by freedom fighters, and a reported visit by Netaji.
tips.good: The history and atmosphere. You are unlikely to find a crowd.
tips.watch: Details come mainly from family accounts, so treat the dates as tradition.
tips.tip: Ask the family about the tunnel stories if there's a quiet moment.

notes: 47 Pathuriaghata Street. Dhunuchi Nach every evening at approx. 7 pm. Suggested on Saptami.
blurb: The Khelat Ghosh family house at 47 Pathuriaghata Street (Google Maps lists it as Pathuriaghata Rajbari), known for what is often called the grandest thakur dalan in the city, about 80 ft of marble.

tips.expect: A long marble corridor and a grand dancing hall (now the Khelat Ghosh Memorial Hall). Rituals include the ablution of the nine-leaf Naba Patrika at the house. The evening dhunuchi dance is the highlight.
tips.good: The 7 pm dhunuchi nach, then a slow walk through the marble hall. The family also offers homemade sweets to the goddess.
tips.watch: Arrive 20 to 30 minutes early on Saptami to get a decent view.
tips.tip: Plan Pathuriaghata as your last North Kolkata stop so you can stay for the dance.

tips.expect: A neighbourhood Puja near Kalighat, close to the temple and the metro.
tips.watch: I couldn't find reliable details. Themes change each year.
tips.tip: Good as a first stop out of Kalighat metro before heading to Mudiali and Deshapriya Park.

tips.expect: A neighbourhood Puja in the Kalighat area.
tips.watch: I found no reliable details, and the exact spot on this map is approximate. It is separate from 66 Pally and 68 Pally.
tips.tip: Combine with 66 Pally and 68 Pally in one short walk.

blurb: A Kalighat-area club Puja that has featured Bengali-cuisine and regional-spice themes.

tips.expect: A creative, theme-led pandal, popular with crowds, with media events around it.
tips.good: Tied to the Kalighat circuit, so easy to reach on foot with 64 Pally and Deshapriya Park.
tips.watch: Themes change each year, so don't rely on past ones.
tips.tip: Use Kalighat metro.

notes: Mudiali Park and Mudiali Club are the same pandal.
blurb: A Kalighat club Puja known for pushing creative boundaries. One year's pandal was built as a monastery interior with ornamental prayer wheels.

tips.expect: An inventive, strongly designed pandal, usually with a full interior experience.
tips.good: It often rewards a slow walk through the set, and lights up well in the evening.
tips.watch: It is on the busy south Kalighat route with Deshapriya Park and Singhi Park.
tips.tip: Visit with Deshapriya Park and Tridhara Sammilani, which are nearby.

blurb: A Kalighat Puja known for sculptural work, large mountain-like structures and a theme song each year.

tips.expect: Elaborate set-building with sculptural elements and sound design.
tips.good: The craftsmanship and the musical element.
tips.watch: Themes change every year, and it is busy in the evening.
tips.tip: Kalighat metro is the closest station.

blurb: A legendary Puja committee in the Kalighat area, known for a very large idol and a big-scale set.

tips.expect: One of South Kolkata's biggest draws, with huge queues and a large, imposing idol.
tips.good: The scale of the idol and set, and being in the middle of the Kalighat circuit.
tips.watch: Very crowded on Ashtami and Navami evenings, with one-way queueing.
tips.tip: Go before 6 pm or late at night, and use Kalighat metro. CōLAB Coffee is nearby for a break.

blurb: A well-known club Puja that marked its 75th year in 2025, with a reputation for blending heritage and creative design.

tips.expect: A polished set in a leafy part of Ballygunge, with big crowds in the evening.
tips.good: The design and the area's many cafes.
tips.watch: Themes change every year. It is crowded from early evening.
tips.tip: Combine with Singhi Park, Maddox Square and Hindustan Park, then eat in Gariahat.

blurb: One of the most famous Pujas in South Kolkata, celebrating its 84th year in 2025 and drawing thousands of visitors.

tips.expect: A very popular pandal with long queues and a strong idol.
tips.good: Consistent quality and a reputation for fresh ideas.
tips.watch: Heavy crowds, especially in the evening.
tips.tip: Pair with Hindustan Park, Samaj Sebi and Mudiali, which are close by.

blurb: A Gariahat Puja known for creative themes and for highlighting endangered folk arts. It is surrounded by some of the city's best-loved cafes.

tips.expect: Artistic, craft-driven sets in a neighbourhood that also has Sienna, Marbella's and Bunaphile.
tips.good: The area itself: you can eat, shop and pandal-hop within a few hundred metres.
tips.watch: Busy on weekend evenings and the cafes fill up fast.
tips.tip: Reserve or arrive early for dinner. Jatin Das Park or Rabindra Sarobar are the nearest metros.

blurb: Established in 1935 and a local institution for adda, with a classic ekchala idol in sabeki style. It is known for its lights and for being busy at any hour.

tips.expect: A lively park setting with food stalls and entertainment, popular with college crowds who call it 'the Thek' (the adda spot).
tips.good: The lights, the atmosphere at midnight and dawn, and the ekchala sabeki idol.
tips.watch: It stays crowded late into the night.
tips.tip: Jatin Das Park is the nearest metro. A good place to be after a Gariahat dinner.

blurb: A South Kolkata Puja with a name for creative themes, bamboo construction and an artistic idol, in a lane also known for its music festival.

tips.expect: A well-built set with fine architectural detail in a relatively calm lane.
tips.good: The bamboo structure and the serene-yet-festive feel.
tips.watch: Themes change every year.
tips.tip: Combine with Ballygunge Cultural and Hindustan Park.

tips.expect: A neighbourhood Puja by the Jadavpur 8B bus stand, popular with the university crowd.
tips.watch: I found no reliable details. Themes change yearly.
tips.tip: Pair with South City Mall cafes, or Suruchi Sangha and Ekdalia.

blurb: One of South Kolkata's best-loved Pujas since 1952, with colourful, ambitious sets. Visitors often wait more than an hour to enter.

tips.expect: A riot of colour and light, with a long queue at peak times.
tips.good: The visual impact. It is a favourite on many lists.
tips.watch: Waits of an hour or more are reported, so budget the time.
tips.tip: Go early. Check their social pages for the new theme.

blurb: Founded in 1943 and one of South Kolkata's most popular Pujas, known for tall idols and eye-catching sets that recreate famous temples.

tips.expect: A tall, ornate idol in a large themed set, with a heavy crowd.
tips.good: The recreations of famous temples and the sheer scale.
tips.watch: Long queues and very heavy foot traffic after dark.
tips.tip: Go on a weekday afternoon, or very late. Famous also for its sabeki six-day Puja tradition.

tips.expect: A local Jadavpur-area Puja.
tips.watch: I couldn't find reliable details.
tips.tip: Good for a calm stop when the bigger pandals are packed.

tips.expect: A neighbourhood Puja in leafy Alipore, usually calmer than the clubs of Kalighat and Ballygunge.
tips.watch: I found no reliable details.
tips.tip: Combine with Deshbandhu Park and Netaji Sangha.

tips.expect: An Alipore community Puja.
tips.watch: I couldn't find reliable details.
tips.tip: A relaxed stop, with parking easier than in the busier areas.

tips.expect: An Alipore community Puja.
tips.watch: I found no reliable details. It is not Netaji Jatiya Sebadal, a separate and better-known pandal.
tips.tip: Combine with the other Alipore pandals.

tips.expect: A neighbourhood Puja in Kasba, calmer than the main south circuit.
tips.watch: I found no reliable details.
tips.tip: Combine with Natun Dal, Udichi and Bosepukur Sitala Mandir.

tips.expect: A Kasba neighbourhood Puja.
tips.watch: No reliable details found. Not the Behala Nutan Dal, which is a different club.
tips.tip: A good fit for a quiet Kasba evening.

tips.expect: A Kasba neighbourhood Puja.
tips.watch: No reliable details found.
tips.tip: A calm add-on to Kasba.

blurb: One of the oldest and most respected Pujas of North Kolkata, with more than a century of history. Netaji and Deshbandhu Chittaranjan Das have both been associated with it.

tips.expect: A devotion-first Puja with a simple, strong pandal and a classic idol, rather than a theme spectacle.
tips.good: The idol and the authentic old-Kolkata atmosphere. It is close to Kumartuli.
tips.watch: Lanes around Baghbazar get very full on Ashtami and Navami evenings.
tips.tip: Walk here via Kumartuli and finish at Nobin Chandra Das for sweets.

blurb: A well-known North Kolkata Puja on Hatibagan's busy market streets. In a recent year it used recycled materials and a simple, sober concept.

tips.expect: A busy market-area pandal with a calm, ethereal idol.
tips.good: Hatibagan's street food and shopping lanes are on the doorstep.
tips.watch: The market streets are packed in the evening.
tips.tip: Do it early evening, then walk on to Maniktala or Shyambazar.

blurb: A Puja in the potters' quarter itself, known in recent years for live demonstrations of clay idol making.

tips.expect: Traditional handicraft themes in the neighbourhood where almost every Kolkata idol is made.
tips.good: You get to see artisans at work. Before Puja the lanes are full of half-made idols, which is a rare sight.
tips.watch: The lanes are very narrow and crowded on Puja evenings.
tips.tip: Visit Kumartuli's workshops in the daytime before Mahalaya for the idols, and the pandals in the evening.

tips.expect: A neighbourhood Puja in the idol-makers' quarter, with a strong sense of craft.
tips.good: The idols here are made a few lanes away, and often by the family running the Puja.
tips.watch: Narrow, crowded lanes.
tips.tip: Go with Kumartuli Park, Baghbazar and Ahiritola in one walk.

notes: Neighbourhood inferred from the name; confirm.
blurb: A North Kolkata community Puja with a literary bent. One year's pandal drew on Leela Majumdar's autobiographical sketch 'Pakdondi'.

tips.expect: A thoughtful, themed pandal in the old lanes, with a literary or cultural idea behind the decoration.
tips.good: It is rarely as packed as the big names, and the lanes around are full of old houses.
tips.watch: Themes change every year, and the exact location is approximate on this map.
tips.tip: Combine with Baghbazar and Kumartuli.

blurb: A multi-award-winning North Kolkata Puja, rooted in eco-awareness with renewable lighting and artistic shows.

tips.expect: A polished, creative set with a social or environmental idea and folk or cultural performances.
tips.good: The consistent craftsmanship, and the community feel.
tips.watch: Popular and crowded after dark. A near neighbour, Chaltabagan Sarbojanin, is a separate pandal.
tips.tip: Reach it from Girish Park metro.

blurb: A Maniktala Puja next to Chaltabagan Lohapatty, known for award-winning decoration and folk dances.

tips.expect: Vibrant community-driven celebration with folk dance and decoration.
tips.good: It sits in a cluster of pandals, so you can hop on foot.
tips.watch: Possible overlap with Chaltabagan Lohapatty, depending on how you read the name. Check the exact address before you go.
tips.tip: Do it in the same walk as Bholanath Dham and Maniktala Saha Bari.

blurb: A century-old Puja near Ahiritola, known for classical dance, art exhibitions and a rich traditional setting.

tips.expect: A relatively simple pandal with traditional set-up and cultural programmes.
tips.good: The old-fashioned feel and the cultural events.
tips.watch: Programmes are in Bengali and run in the evening.
tips.tip: Pair it with the Chatu Babu Latu Babu house, on Beadon Street.

blurb: A historic North Kolkata Puja that marked its 100th year in 2025 with a theme conceptualised by the artist Bhabatosh Sutar.

tips.expect: A highly artistic, concept-led pandal with big crowds.
tips.good: The artistic ambition. Bhabatosh Sutar is one of Kolkata's best-known pandal artists.
tips.watch: It draws large crowds, and last year's theme will not be this year's.
tips.tip: Go early evening and leave before the late rush.

blurb: Dum Dum Park Tarun Sangha, known for colourful celebrations and folk performances, and for creative ideas such as a Byomkesh Bakshi theme in one recent year.

tips.expect: A lively, family-friendly Puja with cultural energy.
tips.good: Good for families: wide streets and a festive feel.
tips.watch: It is far north of the rest of the city, so allow time to get there.
tips.tip: Belgachhia metro is the nearest station. Combine it with Shreebhumi and Lake Town.

blurb: A palatial, big-theme Puja in Lake Town that regularly counts among the most visited in the city.

tips.expect: Huge sets, grand lighting, and very long queues.
tips.good: The spectacle: it is the kind of pandal people plan their whole night around.
tips.watch: One of the most crowded pandals. Expect the area to be gridlocked at night and plan your exit.
tips.tip: Go early on a weekday, or after midnight. A nearby cluster includes Lake Town Adhibasi Brinda.

tips.expect: A neighbourhood Puja in the Lalabagan area of North Kolkata.
tips.watch: I found no reliable details, and the theme changes yearly.
tips.tip: A convenient add-on near Shyambazar or Hatibagan.

blurb: A Sealdah-side club Puja running since 1936 and one of the city's biggest. It is known for a giant idol, a new elaborate theme every year and celebrity guests.

tips.expect: A huge themed set with a very large idol and long, slow-moving queues. Estimates put the crowd at tens of thousands an hour at peak.
tips.good: The scale and the surprise of the new theme each year, which is among the most talked about in the city.
tips.watch: Avoid Ashtami and Navami evenings unless you enjoy being in a crush. Keep valuables zipped and agree a meeting point if you're in a group.
tips.tip: Go on a weekday afternoon or after 1 am. Sealdah is the easiest approach, on foot from the metro.

blurb: A College Street Puja set at the edge of the College Square lake, so the lights and the pandal reflect on the water.

tips.expect: A picturesque lakeside pandal next to Kolkata University, with cultural performances and a lively crowd from late afternoon.
tips.good: The lakeside reflections at night, and being able to walk to the College Street book lanes and the Indian Coffee House.
tips.watch: Crowds start building from about 4 pm and the streets become nearly impassable late in the evening.
tips.tip: Come in the morning or early afternoon, then have coffee at Indian Coffee House.

blurb: A big-budget Central Kolkata Puja known for large, intricate set-pieces, often recreating famous monuments.

tips.expect: Grand craftsmanship and heavy queues, especially after dark.
tips.good: The detail in the set and the idol. It is a favourite with artists and photographers.
tips.watch: Counted among the most crowded pandals, so expect long waits and one-way crowd control.
tips.tip: Go early on a weekday. The nearest metro is MG Road.

tips.expect: A neighbourhood community Puja in Taltala, close to Park Street and the Esplanade area.
tips.watch: I couldn't find reliable details. The theme and idol change every year.
tips.tip: Easy to slot in between Park Street cafes and Central Kolkata pandals.

tips.expect: A neighbourhood Puja in Chorbagan, the same area as several Bonedi Baris.
tips.watch: I found no reliable details, and the theme changes every year.
tips.tip: A good add-on while visiting the Chorbagan Sil and Mitra baris.

blurb: A Chetla club Puja noted for very elaborate decoration. One year's idol was adorned with three crore rudraksha beads.

blurb: The College Street Coffee House: a vast, high-ceilinged hall that has hosted Kolkata's students, poets and arguers for generations.

tips.expect: A noisy, nostalgic hall of tables where people argue over cheap coffee. Reported hours are 9 am to 9 pm, and it costs around ₹200 for two.
tips.good: The cutlet is a legend, and the coffee is old-fashioned and cheap. The history is the real draw.
tips.watch: Cash only. It's popular with students, so tables fill up in the late afternoon.
tips.tip: Combine it with College Square and the College Street book lanes. Go before 6 pm and get a table with a view of the hall.

blurb: A Shyambazar eatery of nearly a century, started as the New Punjabi Restaurant and named Golbari for its semicircular facade. It is known for kosha mangsho.

tips.expect: A busy old-Kolkata eatery at the five-point crossing.
tips.good: The kosha mangsho, a slow-cooked, dry mutton curry.
tips.watch: It is crowded at lunch and dinner.
tips.tip: Combine with Adi Haridas Modak in a Shyambazar food stop.
